course.title: The Agentic Bio Fellowship: Offline Multiomic Analysis for Biopharma Data Science
course.description: Privacy-first local multi-agent orchestration for discovery and multiomic tables. Agents plan; Nextflow (DSL2) executes. 6–8 weeks. Individual Innovator ₹1.5L · Enterprise Team ₹5L.

metadata.description:
A 6–8 week live Fellowship for biopharma data-science leads. Same technical core as cohort 1 (Ollama, Docker, Nextflow). Skin: discovery and multiomic analysis behind the firewall — not clinical-genomics pipeline language.

Checkout is out of band for this MVP. Labs 1–3 live in the cohort 1 tree; lab 4 is a synthetic matrix in this folder. Not a medical device.
metadata.requirements:
• Comfortable in Python or R on assay tables
  • Docker on a machine you control (or documented blocker + offline stub)
  • No requirement to send licensed matrices to a public LLM API
metadata.goals:
1. Run a local LLM with an explicit discovery-data boundary
  2. Ship a Dockerized Python + R analysis image
  3. Treat Nextflow as the execution plane
  4. Join a synthetic multiomic matrix locally, with human review before any write
  5. Run a self-correcting EDA loop that stops for a human gate
  6. Deliver one autonomous local pipeline on a synthetic discovery cohort

The failure mode

Public model endpoints and unpublished expression tables, figure drafts, or partner-data use terms do not mix. “The vendor is SOC2” is not permission to leave the firewall. Partner contracts often forbid exactly this kind of off-box processing even when the rows look de-identified to you.

Local-only rule

  • No public cloud LLM APIs for matrices, assay exports, or unpublished figures.
  • Agents may talk about process. They may not be given the payload.

This track uses the same technical core as cohort 1 (Ollama, Docker, Nextflow). The skin is discovery and multiomic analysis behind the firewall — not clinical-genomics pipeline language.

How the live session runs

Ninety minutes on the week’s contract, then the lab is async. Bring a machine you control (or a written blocker plus the offline stub). We will not paste real payloads into a prompt in class.

Not a medical device. Not clinical advice. Labs use synthetic teaching data only.

Pin the image

Python and R in one reproducible image. Discovery teams still do not ship “it works on my laptop.” The image is the runtime you could defend to QA or to a partner auditor.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/02-container-r-python.

docker build -t agenticbio-lab02:local .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" -v "$PWD/outputs:/outputs" agenticbio-lab02:local python /opt/lab/summarize.py
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/data" -v "$PWD/outputs:/outputs" agenticbio-lab02:local Rscript /opt/lab/summarize.R

Acceptance

  • Image builds on your machine (amd64 or arm64)
  • outputs/python_summary.txt and outputs/r_summary.txt exist
  • Host python3 / R are not required to produce those files
  • The Dockerfile pins a digest or a major tag you could defend in an audit

The audit-trail rule

The workflow file is the audit trail for a discovery pipeline, not a chat log. An agent may propose nextflow run; it must not replace the workflow with ad-hoc bash. If a board later asks which image produced a figure, the answer is in Nextflow’s report, not in Slack.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/03-nextflow-execution-plane.

nextflow run main.nf -c nextflow.config

Or:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work nextflow/nextflow:24.10.0 nextflow run main.nf

Acceptance

  • results/summary.txt exists after a clean run
  • main.nf has at least two processes wired by a channel
  • You can explain the audit-trail rule in two sentences

Ninety minutes on the week’s contract, then the lab is async. Bring a machine you control (or a written blocker plus the offline stub). We will not paste real payloads into a prompt in class.

Map tools to list_dir, read_file, run_nextflow, run_container. Deny network except trusted package mirrors. Human gate on any write that would mutate inputs or a LIMS.

Chat is for planning. Files are for evidence. If the only record of a join is a paste from a chatbot, you do not have a discovery pipeline.

Gene × sample table. Teaching data is synthetic only — invented gene ids and sample id SYNTH-DS-001. Not from a trial, not from GEO-as-proxy for partner data.

Do not replace expression.tsv with a real assay export. A future agent may propose the join command; a human must approve any rewrite of the matrix.

Fail, patch, re-run

The agent proposes a fix. A human approves. The container re-runs. Max three iterations, then stop. Do not invent a cloud notebook.

This week’s fixture

Use the broken copy, not the canonical teaching file. Lab: 04-multiomic-local-agent.

python3 join_matrix.py --expr data/broken-expression.tsv --annot data/annotation.tsv --out outputs/joined-broken.tsv

Expected: the run fails or the output is obviously wrong because data/broken-expression.tsv is malformed on purpose. Write a patched copy under outputs/. Do not rewrite the canonical fixture in data/ without an explicit human yes.

What “self-correcting” is not

Unbounded retries against a production work dir. A bounded loop with a human signature on each patch that changes analysis code or inputs.

What belongs in the image

Interpreters, pinned libraries, the join/parse/retrieve script if it is part of the runtime. Anything a second fellow would need without your $HOME.

What is bind-mounted

Input matrices and outputs. Do not bake licensed assay exports into the image. This track’s teaching table is data/expression.tsv (synthetic).

Network

Image build may use a package mirror. Analysis scripts must not call the network. No Enrichr, no STRING, no “just this once” REST annotation.

Lab folder: labs/02-container-r-python.

Minimal DSL2

Two processes wired by a channel: count lines, then write a summary. Use -c nextflow.config so the container image is explicit. If the agent cannot see which image tag ran, you do not have an audit trail.

Channels are the contract between processes. Do not reach into another process’s work directory from a side script. That is how “helpful” agents destroy -resume.

What to run

Lab folder: labs/03-nextflow-execution-plane.

nextflow run main.nf -c nextflow.config

Or:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work nextflow/nextflow:24.10.0 nextflow run main.nf

Acceptance

  • results/summary.txt exists after a clean run
  • main.nf has at least two processes wired by a channel
  • You can explain the audit-trail rule in two sentences

Map tools, deny network

On OpenClaw or an equivalent local runtime, map tools to:

  • list_dir
  • read_file
  • run_nextflow
  • run_container

Deny network except optional package mirrors you already trust. Do not give the agent a general bash tool that can curl Enrichr.

Implementation

Paste a short architecture note into the week-4 assignment: tools allowed, tools denied, and where the human gate sits. The gate sits before any rewrite of a matrix or a board deck.

Never auto-merge

  • A LIMS write-back
  • A board deck with real sample IDs
  • A production Nextflow -resume on licensed assays
  • Rewrites of the canonical expression.tsv

If the patch would do any of those, the loop ends and a human writes the next ticket. Speed is not a reason to skip the gate.
